findings.text: follow-on: reuse - the test declares its own DOCUMENT_KEYS, IDS_KEYS, SIGNAL_KEYS and UNEXPANDED_KEYS beside the identical constants in imas_codex/ids/handoff.py (lines 17-35). A change to the module's key sets would leave the test asserting the old set and passing on a fixture that still matches, so the two copies can drift. Defensible as a cross-repository contract fixture that must not import from the implementation, but the duplication is a conscious choice that is not recorded anywhere.

follow-on: schema - the LinkML schema declares MEMBER_OF on SignalNode.signal_source (range SignalSource), and FacilitySignal declares no such slot, yet the graph stores FacilitySignal-[:MEMBER_OF]->SignalSource (MERGE at imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py:1861, matched at 15+ call sites) and the new builder reads that direction. A graph built or validated from the LinkML schema alone would not create the edge the builder depends on, and the brief's instruction to derive the edge from the schema would not have yielded the edge the runtime uses. Pre-existing divergence, outside this node's write scope.

follow-on: durability - check_handoff_document enforces the exact key set and nonempty strings for signal_id/source_id/target_path (and the unexpanded required keys), but leaves data_source, source_group, source_array, member_identifier and every optional field untyped, so an empty string or a wrongly-typed value passes. The format rule that a value the graph does not hold is written as null rather than guessed is therefore enforced as key presence only, not as value sanity.
